ai.literal: Mean-company will-fear greatness; meanness indeed as-kin having-surrounded will-complete.
ai.translation: Greatness fears the company of the mean, but meanness embraces them as its own kin.
ai.modern: பெருமை குணம் கொண்டவர்கள் சிற்றினத்தாரோடு சேரப் பயப்படுவார்கள். ஆனால் சிறுமை குணம் கொண்டவர்களோ அவர்களைத் தம் உறவினராகக் கருதிச் சூழ்ந்து கொள்வார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts how noble and base people view bad company. Greatness naturally fears and avoids the company of the mean, knowing it degrades one's character. In contrast, meanness actively seeks out such company, embracing them as if they were family. The word 'சுற்றமா' (as kin) highlights how deeply base individuals attach themselves to bad influences.

ai.literal: of the land by the nature water having changed like that it will become to people of the company that which has the nature will become knowledge
ai.translation: Water changes and takes on the nature of the soil it flows through. Likewise, the mindset of people takes on the nature of the company they keep.
ai.modern: நிலத்தின் தன்மைக்கு ஏற்ப நீர் தன் குணம் மாறி அந்த நிலத்தின் தன்மையை அடையும். அதுபோலவே, மனிதர்களின் அறிவும் அவர்கள் சேர்ந்திருக்கும் கூட்டத்தின் தன்மைக்கு ஏற்ப மாறும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a simple natural analogy to explain how human character is shaped by association. Rainwater is naturally pure, but when it flows over soil, it absorbs the soil's color, taste, and qualities. Similarly, a person's natural intelligence and mindset ('அறிவு') are inevitably altered by the people they choose to associate with ('இனம்'). Therefore, one's character ultimately reflects the nature of their companions.

ai.literal: By the mind becomes to people understanding; by the company becomes 'such a man' thus-called word.
ai.translation: People's natural understanding comes from their own minds, but their reputation as 'such and such a person' comes from the company they keep.
ai.modern: மனிதர்களுக்கு இயற்கையான அறிவு அவர்களின் மனத்தால் உண்டாகும். ஆனால், இவர் இத்தகையவர் என்று உலகத்தாரால் சொல்லப்படும் சொல் அவர்கள் சேர்ந்திருக்கும் கூட்டத்தால் உண்டாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet draws a clear distinction between a person's innate intellect and their social identity. The word 'உணர்ச்சி' refers to the natural understanding or consciousness that arises from one's own mind ('மனத்தான்'). However, the reputation or public judgment that defines a person as being of a certain character ('இன்னான் எனப்படும் சொல்') is entirely shaped by the company they keep ('இனத்தான்'). This emphasizes that while intelligence is personal, character and reputation are judged by one's associations.

ai.literal: Showing as if it exists in the mind, to a person, wisdom becomes that which exists in the company.
ai.translation: Though a person's wisdom appears to originate from their own mind, it actually takes the nature of the company they keep.
ai.modern: ஒருவருடைய அறிவு அவருடைய மனத்திலேயே இயல்பாக இருப்பது போலத் தோன்றினாலும், உண்மையில் அது அவர் சேர்ந்திருக்கும் கூட்டத்தின் தன்மையைப் பொறுத்தே அமையும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the profound influence of one's associates on their intellect. While a person's wisdom might appear to be an independent quality originating from their own mind, it is fundamentally shaped by their social circle. The word 'இனத்து' (in the company) contrasts with 'மனத்து' (in the mind) to emphasize that external associations override internal disposition. Therefore, keeping good company is essential for cultivating true wisdom.

ai.literal: Mind purity, action done purity, both, company purity depending on will come.
ai.translation: Purity of mind and purity of action—both will come depending on the purity of one's company.
ai.modern: மனத்தின் தூய்மை, செய்யும் செயலின் தூய்மை ஆகிய இரண்டும் ஒருவன் சேர்ந்திருக்கும் கூட்டத்தின் தூய்மையைச் சார்ந்தே உண்டாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how deeply a person's associates influence their inner and outer life. It pairs 'மனம் தூய்மை' (purity of mind) with 'செய்வினை தூய்மை' (purity of action), showing that good thoughts and good deeds go together. The word 'தூவா' means 'depending on' or 'supported by'. Thus, the text asserts that these two virtues are not entirely independent, but arise and are sustained by the purity of the company one keeps.

ai.literal: Mind to the pure ones, legacy good will become; company to the pure ones, there is not good not-becoming action.
ai.translation: For those of pure mind, their legacy will be good. For those of pure company, there is no deed that does not turn out good.
ai.modern: மனம் தூய்மையாக உள்ளவர்களுக்கு அவர்கள் விட்டுச்செல்லும் சந்ததியும் நன்மையாக அமையும். சேரும் இனம் தூய்மையாக உள்ளவர்களுக்கு நன்மையாக முடியாத செயல் என்று எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the benefits of a pure mind with those of pure company. The word 'eccam' literally means 'what is left behind', which in this context refers to one's offspring or legacy; for those with a pure mind, this legacy will be good. However, the couplet emphasizes the greater power of good company by stating that for those whose associations are pure, absolutely no action will fail to produce good results. While mental purity secures what follows in the future, pure company guarantees goodness and success in every present deed.

ai.literal: Goodness of mind to enduring lives (is) prosperity; goodness of company all fame will give.
ai.translation: Goodness of mind brings prosperity to living beings, but goodness of company will bring them every kind of fame.
ai.modern: ஒருவருக்கு மனத்தின் நலம் செல்வத்தைத் தரும்; ஆனால் அவர் சேர்ந்திருக்கும் இனத்தின் நலம் அவருக்கு எல்லாப் புகழையும் தேடித்தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the benefits of a good mind with those of good company. While having a good mind brings personal prosperity and well-being to a person, associating with good company elevates them further. Good company brings universal praise and all kinds of fame. The poet emphasizes that while internal goodness is essential for success, the right social circle is what secures lasting honor and reputation.

ai.translation: Even if noble people possess great goodness of mind, the goodness of their company provides them with added protection.
ai.modern: சான்றோர்கள் சிறந்த மனநலத்தை முழுமையாகப் பெற்றிருந்தாலும், அவர்களுக்கு நல்லினத்தின் சேர்க்கையே மேலும் பாதுகாப்பைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that inner virtue alone is not always enough; the external environment matters greatly. Even for noble individuals who already possess a strong, good mind (மனநலம்), being in good company (இனநலம்) acts as a necessary fortress. The word 'ஏமாப்பு' signifies a safeguard or reinforcement, showing that good associations secure and strengthen one's inherent virtues against negative influences.

ai.translation: A good future life is achieved through goodness of mind; moreover, even that goodness is strengthened by the goodness of one's company.
ai.modern: ஒருவனுக்கு மறுமை இன்பம் அவனது மனநலத்தால் உண்டாகும்; அந்த மனநலமும் அவன் சேர்ந்திருக்கும் நல்லினத்தின் நன்மையால் மேலும் வலிமை பெறும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the relationship between a pure mind and good company. While a good mind secures well-being in the future life, that very goodness of mind is reinforced and protected by associating with good people. The word 'ஏமாப்பு' means strength or security, highlighting that even internal virtue requires the external support of good company to remain steadfast.

ai.literal: Than good company even greater support there is not; than bad company sorrow that which causes even there is not.
ai.translation: There is no greater support than good company, and nothing causes more sorrow than bad company.
ai.modern: நல்ல கூட்டத்தை விட சிறந்த துணை வேறு இல்லை. தீய கூட்டத்தை விட துன்பம் தருவது வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the profound effects of good and bad company on a person's life. The word 'நல்லினம்' refers to a group of virtuous people, which acts as the greatest support ('துணை') one can have. Conversely, 'தீயினம்' means a group of wicked people, which is identified as the ultimate source of sorrow ('அல்லல்'). The poet uses a perfectly balanced parallel structure to emphasize that just as nothing helps you more than good friends, nothing harms you more than bad ones.
